XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Yn y fersiwn ddwyieithog, mae’r golofn chwith yn cynnwys yr iaith a lefarwyd yn y cyfarfod. Mae’r golofn dde yn cynnwys cyfieithiad o’r areithiau hynny.

Mae [R] yn dynodi bod yr Aelod wedi datgan buddiant wrth gyflwyno’r busnes.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
In the bilingual version, the left-hand column includes the language used during the meeting. The right-hand column includes a translation of those speeches.

[R] indicates that the Member has declared an interest when tabling the business.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Senedd met in the Chamber and by video-conference at 13:30 with the Llywydd (Huw Irranca-Davies) in the Chair.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cludiant Ysgol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: School Transport

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 1. Pa asesiad mae'r Llywodraeth wedi'i wneud i ganfod a yw'r trefniadau cludiant ysgol presennol yn diwallu anghenion disgyblion ag anghenion dysgu ychwanegol yn Afan Ogwr Rhondda? OQ64716
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 1. What assessment has the Government made of whether current school transport arrangements meet the needs of pupils with additional learning needs in Afan Ogwr Rhondda? OQ64716

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Prynhawn da. Er mai cyfrifoldeb yr awdurdodau lleol yn Afan Ogwr Rhondda ydy asesu anghenion cludiant disgyblion i’r ysgol, mi ydyn ni fel Llywodraeth wrth gwrs yn awyddus i weld darpariaeth effeithiol sy’n diwallu anghenion pawb. Mae hyn yn bwysicach fyth i ddisgyblion efo anghenion dysgu ychwanegol, gan fod cludiant yn gallu bod yn rhwystr gwirioneddol iddyn nhw allu cael mynediad at yr addysg y maen nhw ei hangen.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Good afternoon. Whilst it's for the local authorities in Afan Ogwr Rhondda to assess the school transport needs of all pupils, we as a Government are of course keen to see effective provision that meets everyone’s needs. This is of even greater importance for pupils with additional learning needs, because transport can be a real barrier to them accessing the education that they need.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Mae cyngor Rhondda Cynon Taf wedi cadw cludiant ysgol tybiedig ar gyfer rhai o'r dysgwyr mwyaf agored i niwed, gan gynnwys y rheini ag anghenion dysgu ychwanegol. Ar yr un pryd, mae cost gyffredinol cludiant o'r cartref i'r ysgol yn Rhondda Cynon Taf yn cynyddu yn sylweddol, o £10.5 miliwn yn 2021-22 i £16.9 miliwn yn y rhagolygon ar gyfer 2025-26. Gwyddom fod gan rai dysgwyr ag anghenion dysgu ychwanegol anghenion cludiant mwy cymhleth nag eraill ac y gall cludiant priodol fod yn hanfodol i sicrhau eu bod yn gallu mynd i’w haddysg. A all y Prif Weinidog esbonio sut mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn cydweithio ag awdurdodau lleol i sicrhau eu bod yn cael y cyllid sydd ei angen i barhau i ateb anghenion cludiant gwahanol disgyblion ag anghenion dysgu ychwanegol?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, First Minister. Rhondda Cynon Taf council has retained discretionary school transport for some of its most vulnerable learners, including those with additional learning needs. At the same time, the general cost of transport from home to school in Rhondda Cynon Taf has increased significantly, from £10.5 million in 2021-22 to £16.9 million according to forecasts for 2025-26. We know that some learners with additional learning needs have more complex transport needs than others and that suitable transport arrangements can be vital to ensure that they can access their education. Can the First Minister explain how the Welsh Government is working with local authorities to ensure that they receive the funding that they need to continue to meet the different transport needs of pupils with additional learning needs?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Dwi'n croesawu penderfyniad Rhondda Cynon Taf i gario ymlaen efo darpariaeth trafnidiaeth dewisol—discretionary, felly—ar gyfer rhai o’r dysgwyr mwyaf bregus. Rydyn ni’n sicr yn cydnabod bod trafnidiaeth i ddysgwyr efo anghenion dysgu ychwanegol yn gallu bod yn fwy cymhleth yn aml iawn, yn golygu’r angen am gerbydau arbenigol o bosib neu gynhorthwy gan eraill. Ac mae’n rhaid, wrth gwrs, yn y cyd-destun hwnnw, i benderfyniadau ystyried cynaliadwyedd hirdymor, tra'n cadw’r ffocws yna ar y canlyniadau rydyn ni angen eu gweld rŵan, yn sicrhau bod dysgwyr, uwchlaw popeth, yn gallu cael mynediad at addysg, ac yn gallu gwneud hynny yn rheolaidd a chymryd rhan yn llawn mewn bywyd ysgol.

Mi gafodd anghenion dysgu ychwanegol a thrafnidiaeth ei drafod efo arweinyddion llywodraeth leol ym mis Medi, efo’r WLGA. Mi rydyn ni'n parhau i weithio’n agos efo’r WLGA i gryfhau teithio i ddysgwyr ac i ymateb hefyd i newidiadau mewn patrymau ledled Cymru.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I welcome the decision made by Rhondda Cynon Taf to retain its discretionary transport provision for some of the most vulnerable learners. We certainly recognise that transport to school for pupils with ALN can often be much more complex, as it can perhaps require specialist vehicles or assistance from others. And in that context, of course, decisions must take into account the long-term sustainability, whilst retaining that focus on the results that we need to see now, ensuring that pupils, above all else, can access education, and can do that regularly and take a full part in school life. 

Additional learning needs and transport were discussed with leaders of local authorities in September, along with the Welsh Local Government Association. And we are continuing to work closely with the WLGA to strengthen learner travel provision and also to respond to changes in patterns across Wales.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Parents across Afan Ogwr Rhondda are deeply concerned about their children's school transport arrangements. A survey conducted, with 176 respondents from Rhondda Cynon Taf, found that 72 respondents reported attendance disruption for their children due to insufficient school transport arrangements. A hundred and twenty-five people described feeling anxiety, vulnerability, stress or fear as a result. Reliability, capacity and safety are seriously important, especially when a child faces additional barriers to their learning. So, when assessments are made on transport provision, what will your Government do to ensure that vulnerable learners are not left behind by decisions that are driven by costs rather than outcomes?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae rhieni ar draws Afan Ogwr Rhondda yn bryderus iawn am drefniadau cludiant i'r ysgol eu plant. Fe wnaeth arolwg a gynhaliwyd, â 176 o ymatebwyr o Rondda Cynon Taf, ganfod bod 72 o ymatebwyr wedi hysbysu am darfu ar bresenoldeb eu plant oherwydd trefniadau cludiant i'r ysgol annigonol. Dywedodd cant dau ddeg a phump o bobl eu bod wedi teimlo gorbryder, eu bod yn agored i niwed, straen neu ofn o ganlyniad. Mae dibynadwyedd, capasiti a diogelwch yn bwysig dros ben, yn enwedig pan fydd plentyn yn wynebu rhwystrau ychwanegol i'w ddysgu. Felly, pan fydd asesiadau yn cael eu cynnal ar ddarpariaeth o drafnidiaeth, beth fydd eich Llywodraeth yn ei wneud i sicrhau nad yw dysgwyr agored i niwed yn cael eu gadael ar ôl gan benderfyniadau sy'n cael eu hysgogi gan gostau yn hytrach na chanlyniadau?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: As I said earlier, this is very much a live issue, making sure that, when it comes to additional learning needs learners in particular, those particular circumstances that are relevant to them are taken into account. Funding for school transport, remember, comes through the revenue support grant. It is for local authorities to make provision, but the rise in school transport costs is a complex issue. It is driven by a number of factors. And whether that's local government or the Welsh Government, and the way we interact with this, addressing those complexities requires action across portfolios at local and national level. We, as I say, have been discussing with the WLGA those kinds of pressures that we realise are on local government, at the same time as making the case to the UK Government on the issues that they can take decisions to address—on fuel costs, for example. So, this is something that needs to be addressed on many, many levels.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fel y dywedais i yn gynharach, mae hwn yn sicr yn fater byw, gan wneud yn siŵr, o ran dysgwyr anghenion dysgu ychwanegol yn arbennig, bod yr amgylchiadau penodol hynny sy'n berthnasol iddyn nhw yn cael eu cymryd i ystyriaeth. Mae cyllid ar gyfer cludiant i'r ysgol, cofiwch, yn dod drwy'r grant cynnal refeniw. Mater i awdurdodau lleol yw gwneud darpariaeth, ond mae'r cynnydd i gostau cludiant i'r ysgol yn fater cymhleth. Mae'n cael ei ysgogi gan nifer o ffactorau. A pha un a yw hynny'n fater o lywodraeth leol neu Lywodraeth Cymru, a'r ffordd yr ydym ni'n rhyngweithio â hyn, mae mynd i'r afael â'r cymhlethdodau hynny yn gofyn am weithredu ar draws portffolios ar lefel leol a chenedlaethol. Rydym ni, fel y dywedais i, wedi bod yn trafod gyda CLlLC y mathau hynny o bwysau yr ydym ni'n sylweddoli sydd ar lywodraeth leol, ar yr un pryd â gwneud y ddadl i Lywodraeth y DU ar y materion y gallan nhw wneud penderfyniadau i fynd i'r afael â nhw—ar gostau tanwydd, er enghraifft. Felly, mae hyn yn rhywbeth y mae angen mynd i'r afael ag ef ar lawer iawn o lefelau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Ynni Cymunedol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Community Energy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 2. Pa gamau mae'r Llywodraeth yn eu cymryd i gefnogi'r gwaith o greu prosiectau ynni cymunedol a sicrhau bod manteision adnoddau naturiol Cymru yn cael eu cadw yng Nghymru? OQ64708
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 2. What action is the Government taking to support the creation of community energy projects and ensure that the benefits of Wales’s natural resources are retained in Wales? OQ64708

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Welsh Government investment through Ynni Cymru is generating real savings and benefits for the community. I was delighted just a few weeks ago to visit the Iqra Masjid mosque in Newport to see one project first-hand for myself. Our plans to establish a new Welsh public energy company will support our ambition in the national energy strategy for more of the energy generated in Wales to be owned in Wales and to benefit Wales. More Welsh ownership will see the value created from our natural resources retained for the people of Wales, which is something I hope all of us would want to pursue.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae buddsoddiad Llywodraeth Cymru drwy Ynni Cymru yn cynhyrchu arbedion a manteision gwirioneddol i'r gymuned. Roeddwn i wrth fy modd ychydig wythnosau yn ôl o ymweld â mosg Iqra Masjid yng Nghasnewydd i weld un prosiect yn bersonol drosof fy hun. Bydd ein cynlluniau i sefydlu cwmni ynni cyhoeddus newydd yng Nghymru yn cefnogi ein huchelgais yn y strategaeth ynni genedlaethol i fwy o'r ynni a gynhyrchir yng Nghymru fod yn eiddo i Gymru ac i fod er budd Cymru. Bydd mwy o berchnogaeth yng Nghymru yn golygu bod y gwerth sy'n cael ei greu o'n hadnoddau naturiol yn cael ei gadw i bobl Cymru, sy'n rhywbeth yr wyf i'n gobeithio y byddai pob un ohonom ni eisiau mynd ar ei drywydd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, I'm proud to support a grass-roots campaign in Pen-y-bont Bro Morgannwg to stop the proposed small modular reactor nuclear project in the Llynfi valley by Last Energy. More extractive and harmful projects are not what our post-industrial communities deserve. It's no surprise why they have selected one of our most deprived communities to pilot this new nuclear technology. Campaigners across the constituency are calling out for renewable energy projects that they can directly benefit from, and that's why we're exploring alternative energy options within the constituency rather than accepting private organisations coming in to extract the profits from our communities. So, Prif Weinidog, will you reaffirm this Government's ambition to ensure that our communities benefit from energy projects?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, rwy'n falch o gefnogi ymgyrch llawr gwlad ym Mhen-y-bont Bro Morgannwg i atal y prosiect niwclear adweithydd modiwlaidd bach arfaethedig yng nghwm Llynfi gan Last Energy. Nid prosiectau mwy cloddiol a niweidiol yw'r hyn y mae ein cymunedau ôl-ddiwydiannol yn ei haeddu. Nid yw'n syndod pam maen nhw wedi dewis un o'n cymunedau mwyaf difreintiedig i dreialu'r dechnoleg niwclear newydd hon. Mae ymgyrchwyr ar draws yr etholaeth yn galw am brosiectau ynni adnewyddadwy y gallan nhw elwa ohonyn nhw yn uniongyrchol, a dyna pam rydym ni'n archwilio opsiynau ynni amgen o fewn yr etholaeth yn hytrach na derbyn sefydliadau preifat yn dod i mewn i dynnu'r elw o'n cymunedau. Felly, Brif Weinidog, a wnewch chi ailddatgan uchelgais y Llywodraeth hon i sicrhau bod ein cymunedau yn elwa o brosiectau ynni?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Yes, absolutely. In many ways, that principle is agnostic of that source of power generation. Energy projects in Wales must show, I think, how they improve matters for people in Wales. It's an important issue that will be at the heart of the national energy strategy we have committed to delivering. Through that strategy, we will deliver that commitment to make sure that Welsh people and communities have more ownership, as I say, of energy initiatives, and that they and their communities receive also their fair share of the profits. We need a balanced energy system that delivers secure supply. Renewables will be an important part of that system, obviously. The public energy company that we're currently consulting on will have a vital role, I think, to play in supporting communities and securing value from commercially led projects too.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Gwnaf, yn sicr. Mewn sawl ffordd, mae'r egwyddor honno yn agnostig ar y ffynhonnell honno o gynhyrchu pŵer. Mae'n rhaid i brosiectau ynni yng Nghymru ddangos, rwy'n credu, sut maen nhw'n gwella pethau i bobl yng Nghymru. Mae'n fater pwysig a fydd yn ganolog i'r strategaeth ynni genedlaethol yr ydym ni wedi ymrwymo i'w chyflawni. Drwy'r strategaeth honno, byddwn yn cyflawni'r ymrwymiad hwnnw i wneud yn siŵr bod gan bobl a chymunedau Cymru fwy o berchnogaeth, fel y dywedais i, o fentrau ynni, a'u bod nhw a'u cymunedau hefyd yn derbyn eu cyfran deg o'r elw. Mae angen system ynni gytbwys arnom ni, sy'n darparu cyflenwad diogel. Bydd ynni adnewyddadwy yn rhan bwysig o'r system honno, yn amlwg. Bydd gan y cwmni ynni cyhoeddus yr ydym ni'n ymgynghori arno ar hyn o bryd ran hanfodol i'w chwarae, rwy'n credu, o ran gefnogi cymunedau a sicrhau gwerth o brosiectau dan arweiniad masnachol hefyd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, Wales presently has nearly 4,000 MW of installed capacity, all dependent on gas for firing. Given what's just been said, this document, produced by the National Grid, 'Community Energy Scenarios', reveals the truth of this community energy nonsense. At best—at best—it will mean we go from 47 MW to 281 MW by 2035. To be fair to you, you're not a Nimby First Minister, but what I would describe Plaid's nuclear policy as is 'only in Rhun's back yard', because that's effectively what we've got. First Minister, right across south Wales, we have a growing energy problem. Will you reconsider Plaid's energy policy so that we can look at a series of small modular reactors right across south Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, ar hyn o bryd mae gan Gymru bron i 4,000 MW o gapasiti wedi'i osod, y cwbl yn dibynnu ar nwy i'w danio. O ystyried yr hyn sydd newydd gael ei ddweud, mae'r ddogfen hon, a luniwyd gan y Grid Cenedlaethol, 'Community Energy Scenarios', yn datgelu gwirionedd y nonsens ynni cymunedol hwn. O'r ochr orau—o'r ochr orau—bydd yn golygu ein bod ni'n mynd o 47 MW i 281 MW erbyn 2035. I fod yn deg â chi, dydych chi ddim yn Brif Weinidog Nimby, ond byddwn yn disgrifio polisi niwclear Plaid Cymru fel 'dim ond yn ngardd gefn Rhun', oherwydd dyna sydd gennym ni i bob pwrpas. Brif Weinidog, ledled de Cymru gyfan, mae gennym ni broblem ynni gynyddol. A wnewch chi ailystyried polisi ynni Plaid Cymru fel y gallwn edrych ar gyfres o adweithyddion modiwlaidd bach ledled de Cymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Will we reconsider our energy strategy? I think I've confirmed again today that we are bringing forward a new national energy strategy that calls for that balanced energy system. Referring to community energy 'nonsense'—talk to people in Bethesda about the 'nonsense' that is their energy production scheme, which they are hugely proud of and that brings all sorts of benefits to that community. Look at all those projects across Wales, including the one I visited in Newport recently, that people take a real, genuine sense of ownership of and know that they are tackling the energy crisis that we are facing, plus the climate change crisis that his party is denying. Our energy future will bring together all sorts of technologies, all sorts of production methods. I want to use our resources for the benefit of the people of Wales, but at the heart of that has to be something that is very different to the extractive story of the past and that has the interests of Wales at the very heart of it—something that Reform really struggle with.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: A wnawn ni ailystyried ein strategaeth ynni? Rwy'n credu fy mod i wedi cadarnhau eto heddiw ein bod ni'n cyflwyno strategaeth ynni genedlaethol newydd sy'n galw am y system ynni gytbwys honno. Gan gyfeirio at 'nonsens' ynni cymunedol—siaradwch â phobl ym Methesda am 'nonsens' eu cynllun cynhyrchu ynni, y maen nhw'n eithriadol o falch ohono ac sy'n cynnig pob math o fanteision i'r gymuned honno. Edrychwch ar yr holl brosiectau hynny ledled Cymru, gan gynnwys yr un yr ymwelais ag ef yng Nghasnewydd yn ddiweddar, y mae pobl yn cymryd ymdeimlad gwirioneddol iawn o berchnogaeth ohonyn nhw ac yn gwybod eu bod nhw'n mynd i'r afael â'r argyfwng ynni sy'n ein hwynebu, yn ogystal â'r argyfwng newid hinsawdd y mae ei blaid ef yn ei wadu. Bydd ein dyfodol ynni yn dwyn â phob math o dechnoleg ynghyd, pob math o ddulliau cynhyrchu. Rwyf i eisiau defnyddio ein hadnoddau er budd pobl Cymru, ond yn ganolog i hynny mae'n rhaid cael rhywbeth sy'n wahanol iawn i hanes cloddio'r gorffennol ac sydd â buddiannau Cymru yn gwbl ganolog iddo—rhywbeth y mae Reform wir yn cael trafferth ag ef.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae cynlluniau egni cymdeithasol, fel cynlluniau mwy, hefyd angen mynediad i'r grid. Dwi eisiau gweld cynlluniau cynaliadwy a'r isadeiledd grid yn cael eu cyflawni ledled Cymru, i gyflawni'r buddiannau rydyn ni eisiau eu gweld ar gyfer ein cymunedau lleol.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Community energy schemes, like larger schemes, also require access to the grid. I want to see sustainable schemes and the grid infrastructure being delivered across Wales in order to deliver the benefits that we want to see for our local communities.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, what steps are you taking, working with the UK Government, Ofgem and network operators, to ensure that connection costs and waiting times don't prevent these projects, be they community or larger scale, from progressing? We need that grid infrastructure in place for it to succeed. I think Wales has got an opportunity to be an energy superpower, and that's why the comments from the Plaid Cymru Member earlier about SMRs are so disappointing. So, can you, further to my first question, explain why SMRs are the right solution for Anglesey but not for south Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, pa gamau ydych chi'n eu cymryd, gan weithio gyda Llywodraeth y DU, Ofgem a gweithredwyr rhwydwaith, i sicrhau nad yw costau cysylltu ac amseroedd aros yn atal y prosiectau hyn, pa un a ydyn nhw'n gymunedol neu ar raddfa fwy, rhag symud ymlaen? Mae angen y seilwaith grid hwnnw ar waith arnom ni er mwyn iddo lwyddo. Rwy'n credu bod gan Gymru gyfle i fod yn archbŵer ynni, a dyna pam mae'r sylwadau gan Aelod Plaid Cymru yn gynharach am Ofynion Rheoli Statudol mor siomedig. Felly, a allwch chi, gan ymhelaethu ar fy nghwestiwn cyntaf, esbonio pam mai Gofynion Rheoli Statudol yw'r ateb cywir ar gyfer Ynys Môn ond nid ar gyfer de Cymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I ateb y cwestiwn yna, mae hwn yn dechnoleg sydd yn datblygu, ac mae o'n gwneud synnwyr i'w ddatblygu ar safle lle mae yna sgiliau niwclear o'r gorffennol. Ond mae'r cwestiwn yn ehangach na hynny, wrth gwrs. Dwi ddim yn meddwl bod yna lawer o anghytuno rhyngom ni, mewn difri, ar yr angen i wneud yn fawr o'n hadnoddau naturiol ni fel gwlad, i sicrhau ein bod ni'n gallu cynhyrchu mwy o ynni yn defnyddio'n adnoddau naturiol ni, pa un ai yn wynt neu'n donnau neu'n llanw, neu beth bynnag.

Dwi'n cytuno hefyd ar yr angen i sicrhau bod y system sydd gennym ni i drosglwyddo a dosbarthu'r trydan yna yn wydn ar gyfer y dyfodol. Rydyn ni'n mynd i fod angen llawer mwy o drydan yn y dyfodol, ac mae'n rhaid i'r trydan yna gyrraedd ein cymunedau ni a gadael y llefydd lle mae'n cael ei gynhyrchu. Ond, unwaith eto, dwi'n dod yn ôl at y pwynt canolog yma fod modd gwneud hynny mewn cydweithrediad efo ein cymunedau ni, yn gwneud yn siŵr nad oes yna ecsbloetio. Hefyd, dwi'n cytuno ar y ffaith bod hynny'n gorfod digwydd mewn cydweithrediad efo Llywodraeth y Deyrnas Unedig, ac yn y blaen. Felly, mae yna agenda yn fan hyn. Dwi'n gobeithio y gallwn ni adeiladu consensws drosto fo. Mae yna benderfyniadau anodd ynghlwm wrtho, ond adeiladu dyfodol ynni annibynnol ar gyfer ein hunain fel gwlad yr ydym ni a'r holl fuddiannau a fydd yn llifo o hynny.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
To answer that question, this is a developing technology, and it makes sense to develop it on a site where past nuclear skills exist. But the question is broader than that, of course. I don't think that there's a great deal of disagreement between us, truth be told, on the need to make the most of our natural resources as a nation, to ensure that we can produce more energy using our natural resources, be that wind, wave, tide or whatever.

I agree also on the need to ensure that the system that we have to distribute that electricity should be resilient for the future. We're going to need a lot more electricity in the future, and that electricity has to get to our communities and leave the sites of production. But, once again, I return to this central point that that can be done in collaboration with our communities, ensuring that there is no exploitation. I also agree with the fact that that has to happen in collaboration with the UK Government, and so on. So, there is an agenda here. I hope we can build consensus on it. There will be difficult decisions in relation to that agenda, but we are building an independent energy future for ourselves as a nation, along with all the benefits that will flow from that.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Galwaf yn awr ar arweinwyr y pleidiau i holi'r Prif Weinidog. Yn gyntaf, arweinydd Reform UK, Helen Jenner.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I now call the party leaders to question the First Minister. First of all, the leader of Reform UK, Helen Jenner.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Lywydd. First Minister, I want to raise a deeply disturbing case from our capital city. In March this year, 29-year-old Mohammed Abbas arrived in Britain on a small boat from France. By June, he was in custody facing criminal charges. In July, he was convicted of offences including assaulting a police officer and sentenced to 300 hours of community service. He was subsequently placed in Home Office-funded accommodation in Cardiff. Just two days later, at 2 o'clock in the morning, he entered a family home and committed sexual offences in the presence of two young girls, both under the age of 16. He has since pleaded guilty to four further offences and is awaiting sentencing. Those two young girls should have been safe in their own home. First Minister, what discussions have you had with the Home Office about this case? What assurances have you sought about the safeguarding of communities hosting asylum accommodation? And will you now commission an urgent review of the arrangements between Welsh public services and the Home Office to ensure that a case like this is never repeated?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. Brif Weinidog, hoffwn godi achos hynod annymunol o'n prifddinas. Ym mis Mawrth eleni, cyrhaeddodd y dyn 29 oed, Mohammed Abbas, Brydain ar gwch bach o Ffrainc. Erbyn mis Mehefin, roedd yn y ddalfa yn wynebu cyhuddiadau troseddol. Ym mis Gorffennaf, fe'i cafwyd yn euog o droseddau a oedd yn cynnwys ymosod ar swyddog yr heddlu a'i ddedfrydu i 300 awr o wasanaeth cymunedol. Cafodd ei leoli wedi hynny mewn llety a wedi'i ariannu gan y Swyddfa Gartref yng Nghaerdydd. Dim ond dau ddiwrnod yn ddiweddarach, am 2 o'r gloch y bore, aeth i mewn i gartref teuluol a chyflawni troseddau rhywiol ym mhresenoldeb dwy ferch ifanc, y ddwy o dan 16 oed. Ers hynny, mae wedi pledio'n euog i bedair trosedd arall ac yn aros i gael ei ddedfrydu. Dylai'r ddwy ferch ifanc hynny fod wedi bod yn ddiogel yn eu cartref eu hunain. Brif Weinidog, pa drafodaethau ydych chi wedi eu cael gyda'r Swyddfa Gartref am yr achos hwn? Pa sicrwydd ydych chi wedi gofyn amdano am ddiogelu cymunedau lle ceir llety lloches? Ac a wnewch chi gomisiynu nawr adolygiad brys o'r trefniadau rhwng gwasanaethau cyhoeddus Cymru a'r Swyddfa Gartref i sicrhau nad yw achos fel hwn byth yn cael ei ailadrodd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I think I would refer the Member to the safeguarding work that this Government is doing in general, making sure that we are strengthening the provisions that we put in place as a Welsh Government to safeguard the citizens of Wales. What has been described to me—and it's not a case that I am familiar with myself—is criminality. What has been described to me are the actions of an individual that all of us would condemn and that the legal system should be empowered to deal with.

I know that it is always the case that Reform seeks only to comment on those elements of criminality that emerge from people who have come into the UK, but that really doesn't help us when it comes to the core issue here, which is to make sure that we in Wales, in the public sector, in the Welsh Government, have safeguarding measures in place across the board that make sure that we de-risk and that we look after those vulnerable people within our society.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n credu y byddwn i'n cyfeirio'r Aelod at y gwaith diogelu y mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn ei wneud yn gyffredinol, gan wneud yn siŵr ein bod ni'n cryfhau'r darpariaethau yr ydym ni'n eu rhoi ar waith fel Llywodraeth Cymru i ddiogelu dinasyddion Cymru. Troseddoldeb yw'r hyn sydd wedi cael ei ddisgrifio i mi—ac nid yw'n achos yr wyf i'n gyfarwydd ag ef fy hun. Gweithredoedd unigolyn y byddai pob un ohonom ni'n eu condemnio ac y dylai'r system gyfreithiol fod wedi ei grymuso i ymdrin â nhw yw'r hyn sydd wedi cael ei ddisgrifio i mi.

Rwy'n gwybod ei bod hi bob amser yn wir bod Reform yn ceisio gwneud sylwadau ar yr elfennau hynny o droseddoldeb sy'n deillio o bobl sydd wedi dod i mewn i'r DU yn unig, ond nid yw hynny'n ein helpu ni mewn gwirionedd pan ddaw i'r mater craidd yma, sef sicrhau bod gennym ni yng Nghymru, yn y sector cyhoeddus, yn Llywodraeth Cymru, fesurau diogelu ar waith yn gyffredinol sy'n sicrhau ein bod ni'n dad-risgio a'n bod ni'n gofalu am y bobl agored i niwed hynny yn ein cymdeithas.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
The point is that we absolutely accept we already have criminals home grown in the country, but why would we risk importing more? People that we don't know—we know nothing about them. The fact is, whether this is an isolated case or not, two girls have suffered because of a serious failure in safeguarding.

First Minister, last week your Deputy Minister for Transport announced yet another 18-month study into congestion on the M4 around Newport, alongside proposals that could see motorway junctions closed. Let's not forget it was the Labour Government who scrapped the relief road, wasting well over £100 million of taxpayers' money in the process. Closing motorway junctions doesn't make the traffic disappear; it simply moves the problem elsewhere, and restricts emergency services trying to carry out their duties. First Minister, Newport needs a long-term solution that improves capacity, not measures that redistribute congestion into residential communities. So, I'll ask you a straightforward question and I expect a straightforward answer: does your Government intend to press ahead with building an M4 relief road around Newport during this Senedd term—yes or no?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Y pwynt yw ein bod ni'n derbyn yn llwyr bod gennym ni droseddwyr cartref yn y wlad eisoes, ond pam fyddem ni'n cymryd y risg o fewnforio mwy? Pobl nad ydym ni'n eu hadnabod—dydyn ni'n gwybod dim byd amdanyn nhw. Y gwir yw, pa un a yw hwn yn achos neilltuol ai peidio, mae dwy ferch wedi dioddef oherwydd methiant difrifol o ran diogelu.

Brif Weinidog, yr wythnos diwethaf cyhoeddodd eich Dirprwy Weinidog Trafnidiaeth astudiaeth 18 mis arall i dagfeydd ar yr M4 o amgylch Casnewydd, ochr yn ochr â chynigion a allai arwain at gau cyffyrdd traffordd. Gadewch i ni beidio ag anghofio mai'r Llywodraeth Lafur wnaeth gefnu ar y ffordd liniaru, gan wastraffu ymhell dros £100 miliwn o arian trethdalwyr wrth wneud hynny. Nid yw cau cyffyrdd traffordd yn gwneud i'r traffig ddiflannu; y cwbl y mae'n ei wneud yw symud y broblem i rywle arall, a chyfyngu'r gwasanaethau brys sy'n ceisio cyflawni eu dyletswyddau. Brif Weinidog, mae angen ateb hirdymor ar Gasnewydd sy'n gwella capasiti, nid mesurau sy'n ailddosbarthu tagfeydd i gymunedau preswyl. Felly, fe wnaf i ofyn cwestiwn syml i chi ac rwy'n disgwyl ateb syml: a yw eich Llywodraeth yn bwriadu bwrw ymlaen ag adeiladu ffordd liniaru'r M4 o amgylch Casnewydd yn ystod y tymor Senedd hwn—ydy neu nac ydy?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I described in the Senedd last week the multiphase approach that we are taking to addressing an issue that previous administrations chose not to. Inaction, we have decided, is not an option for this new Plaid Cymru Government. Therefore, we will press ahead with a number of short-term measures in order to strengthen the infrastructure that is in place now. And we are embarking right away on a piece of work to look at what is that engineering solution that will help then bring together a package that will deal with the blight that is the Brynglas situation for the people of Newport, and the blockage that is in place for the people and the economy of the wider south Wales region.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Disgrifiais yn y Senedd yr wythnos diwethaf y dull aml-gam yr ydym ni'n ei fabwysiadu o fynd i'r afael â mater y dewisodd gweinyddiaethau blaenorol beidio â mynd i'r afael ag ef. Nid yw peidio â gweithredu, rydym ni wedi penderfynu, yn opsiwn i'r Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru newydd hon. Felly, byddwn yn bwrw ymlaen â nifer o fesurau byrdymor er mwyn cryfhau'r seilwaith sydd ar waith rŵan. Ac rydym ni'n cychwyn ar unwaith ar ddarn o waith i edrych ar beth yw'r ateb peirianyddol hwnnw a fydd yn helpu wedyn i ddod â phecyn at ei gilydd a fydd yn delio â melltith sefyllfa Bryn-glas i bobl Casnewydd, a'r rhwystr sy'n bodoli i bobl ac economi rhanbarth ehangach de Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, it's a 'no', and it's a shame to see that you're determined to continue Mark Drakeford's war on motorists. Nothing changes, does it? The cosy Cardiff consensus continues. Speaking of which, First Minister, throughout the Senedd election, you promised Wales you would deliver change, but we've learned this morning that you've done a deal with Labour to push through your failed supplementary budget. When Labour were in power, it was your party that was propping them up, voting through their budgets as they destroyed our public services. Now you're in power, it's Labour who are nodding along as your Government sends millions of pounds abroad while our NHS suffers. When you said you'd deliver change, people expected you to change more than just the seating plan in the Chamber. And I know a few things about seating plans. So, First Minister, how much longer will the people of Wales have to wait for a Government prepared to deliver real change?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, 'nac ydy' yw'r ateb, ac mae'n drueni gweld eich bod chi'n benderfynol o barhau rhyfel Mark Drakeford yn erbyn modurwyr. Does dim byd yn newid, nac oes? Mae'r consensws clyd yng Nghaerdydd yn parhau. Wrth siarad am hynny, Brif Weinidog, trwy gydol etholiad y Senedd, fe wnaethoch chi addo i Gymru y byddech chi'n cyflawni newid, ond rydym ni wedi darganfod y bore yma eich bod chi wedi gwneud cytundeb gyda Llafur i wthio eich cyllideb atodol fethedig drwodd. Pan oedd Llafur mewn grym, eich plaid chi oedd yn eu dal nhw i fyny, gan bleidleisio dros eu cyllidebau wrth iddyn nhw ddinistrio ein gwasanaethau cyhoeddus. Nawr eich bod chi mewn grym, Llafur sy'n nodio gyda chi wrth i'ch Llywodraeth anfon miliynau o bunnoedd dramor tra bod ein GIG yn dioddef. Pan wnaethoch chi ddweud y byddech chi'n cyflawni newid, roedd pobl yn disgwyl i chi newid mwy na dim ond y cynllun seddi yn y Siambr. Ac rwy'n gwybod ambell i beth am gynlluniau seddi. Felly, Brif Weinidog, pa mor hir eto y bydd yn rhaid i bobl Cymru aros am Lywodraeth sy'n barod i gyflawni newid gwirioneddol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
The seating plan on that side of the Chamber seems to be changing every week. [Laughter.] And I would suggest that maybe she doesn't make herself too comfortable where she is either.

We have an agreement in place on the supplementary budget and I'm grateful, on an issue that Reform also wanted us to deliver on, which is additional learning needs. The irony, Llywydd. It's just that Reform enjoys shouting from the sidelines rather than wanting to contribute to the future of Wales. The fact is that this Government has decided to make good on the wishes of the people of the north-west of Wales on the Menai crossing; that this Government is taking action after years of inaction around the M4.

I go back to the second question asked. This ultimately is around dog-whistle politics for Reform. They talk about the risk of importing criminals. And absolutely, we need to take measures to make sure that we keep our citizens safe. But what about the risk of importing doctors? What about the risk of importing nurses? What about the risk of importing people who want to contribute to the life and the future of Wales in a way the benches over there have very, very little interest in doing?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae'n ymddangos bod y cynllun seddi ar yr ochr yna i'r Siambr yn newid bob wythnos. [Chwerthin.] A byddwn yn awgrymu efallai iddi beidio â gwneud ei hun yn rhy gyfforddus lle mae hi chwaith.

Mae gennym ni gytundeb ar waith ar y gyllideb atodol ac rwy'n ddiolchgar, ar fater yr oedd Reform hefyd eisiau i ni gyflawni arno, sef anghenion dysgu ychwanegol. Yr eironi, Lywydd. Dim ond bod Reform yn mwynhau gweiddi o'r ystlys yn hytrach na bod eisiau cyfrannu at ddyfodol Cymru. Y gwir amdani yw bod y Llywodraeth hon wedi penderfynu gwireddu dymuniadau pobl gogledd-orllewin Cymru o ran croesfan Menai; bod y Llywodraeth hon yn gweithredu ar ôl blynyddoedd o ddiffyg gweithredu o amgylch yr M4.

Dychwelaf at yr ail gwestiwn a ofynnwyd. Mae hyn yn ymwneud â gwleidyddiaeth chwiban ci i Reform yn y pen draw. Maen nhw'n siarad am y risg o fewnforio troseddwyr. Ac yn sicr, mae angen i ni gymryd mesurau i wneud yn siŵr ein bod ni'n cadw ein dinasyddion yn ddiogel. Ond beth am y risg o fewnforio meddygon? Beth am y risg o fewnforio nyrsys? Beth am y risg o fewnforio pobl sydd eisiau cyfrannu at fywyd a dyfodol Cymru mewn ffordd y mae gan y meinciau draw yn y fan yna ychydig iawn, iawn o ddiddordeb yn ei wneud?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Arweinydd Llafur Cymru nawr—Ken Skates.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Leader of Welsh Labour now—Ken Skates.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Llywydd. First Minister, some here will doubtless work tirelessly to destroy and sabotage devolution, but Welsh Labour firmly believes in making it work for the people of Wales, and we're proud to have fought for and secured an extra £60 million for children with additional learning needs for this financial year. That's a 50 per cent increase on two weeks ago, and it's £60 million more than at the start of the summer. But, of course, this is only the first step. We believe that more funding should be made available for ALN, and we've made it clear that not a penny of this £60 million should come from elsewhere within the education budget, and we've argued successfully that there needs to be a long-term sustainability plan for further education in Wales. First Minister, will you confirm these commitments today? And also, will you commit to getting the extra £60 million that Welsh Labour has fought for to schools and to children as soon as possible?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. Brif Weinidog, rwy'n siŵr y bydd rhai yma yn gweithio'n ddiflino i ddinistrio a thanseilio datganoli, ond mae Llafur Cymru yn credu'n gryf mewn gwneud iddo weithio i bobl Cymru, ac rydym ni'n falch o fod wedi brwydro i gael £60 miliwn ychwanegol i blant sydd ag anghenion dysgu ychwanegol, a'i sicrhau ar gyfer y flwyddyn ariannol hon. Mae hynny'n gynnydd o 50 y cant o bythefnos yn ôl, ac mae'n £60 miliwn yn fwy nag ar ddechrau'r haf. Ond, wrth gwrs, dim ond y cam cyntaf yw hwn. Rydym ni'n credu y dylid gwneud mwy o gyllid ar gael ar gyfer ADY, ac rydym ni wedi ei gwneud hi'n eglur na ddylai ceiniog o'r £60 miliwn hwn ddod o rywle arall o fewn y gyllideb addysg, ac rydym ni wedi dadlau'n llwyddiannus bod angen cynllun cynaliadwyedd hirdymor ar gyfer addysg bellach yng Nghymru. Brif Weinidog, a wnewch chi gadarnhau'r ymrwymiadau hyn heddiw? A hefyd, a wnewch chi ymrwymo i gael y £60 miliwn ychwanegol y mae Llafur Cymru wedi brwydro drosto i ysgolion ac i blant cyn gynted â phosibl?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: As I said previously, I'm very pleased that an agreement has been reached, and I thank those who engaged very constructively with us to get us to a point where we both now are able to move to release money for additional learning needs services, an area on which we both have common ground. It was a manifesto commitment of mine to move towards sustainability within ALN. That hasn't changed. We want to pursue that sustainability. The discussions that we have been having, without going into confidential issues, have been very much about how we are able to release this money that doesn't come from elsewhere in the education budget. This is mature, positive working, and it has led to what we both wanted to happen—and others in this Chamber—which is the strengthening of ALN provision.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fel y dywedais i yn flaenorol, rwy'n falch iawn ein bod ni wedi dod i gytundeb, a diolchaf i'r rhai a ymgysylltodd yn adeiladol iawn â ni i'n cael ni i bwynt lle mae'r ddau ohonom ni bellach yn gallu cymryd camau i ryddhau arian ar gyfer gwasanaethau anghenion dysgu ychwanegol, maes y mae gan y ddau ohonom ni dir cyffredin arno. Roedd yn un o'm hymrwymiadau maniffesto i symud tuag at gynaliadwyedd ym maes ADY. Nid yw hynny wedi newid. Rydym ni eisiau mynd ar drywydd y cynaliadwyedd hwnnw. Mae'r trafodaethau yr ydym ni wedi bod yn eu cael, heb drafod materion cyfrinachol, wedi ymwneud yn fawr iawn â sut allwn ni ryddhau'r arian hwn nad yw'n dod o rywle arall yn y gyllideb addysg. Mae hyn yn weithio aeddfed, cadarnhaol, ac mae wedi arwain at yr hyn yr oedd y ddau ohonom ni eisiau i ddigwydd—ac eraill yn y Siambr hon—sef cryfhau'r ddarpariaeth ADY.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Absolutely, First Minister, and Welsh Labour will never fold. We will stand firm in our positions, unlike parties—[Interruption.]—unlike parties that have no principles, that have no values, that have no direction, but have plenty of different leaders, it seems. First Minister, of course, ALN-related provision and home-to-school transport are costing more and more each year. It's now reached around £200 million for the taxpayer—money that is coming from education budgets. Now, it may come as a surprise to the vocal crew on the other side of this Chamber, but their leader at a UK level, when he went to Kent, said that spending on home-to-school transport was ridiculous. Actually, he used more profound terms. He said that the way that he would cut it is to stop providing it, to make parents drive or walk their children to school. Is that the policy of Reform here, First Minister, do you think?

And, First Minister, would you agree to a more sensible approach, a more intelligent approach, one that was started by the Welsh Labour Government, where we composed an expert panel, a cross-party, cross-departmental group, to look at how we can reduce costs for home-to-school transport whilst improving the amount of home-to-school transport that can be provided to young people?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Yn sicr, Brif Weinidog, ac ni wnaiff Llafur Cymru byth ildio. Byddwn yn sefyll yn gadarn yn ein safbwyntiau, yn wahanol i bleidiau—[Torri ar draws.]—yn wahanol i bleidiau nad oes ganddyn nhw unrhyw egwyddorion, nad oes ganddyn nhw unrhyw werthoedd, nad oes ganddyn nhw unrhyw gyfeiriad, ond sydd â digon o wahanol arweinwyr, mae'n ymddangos. Brif Weinidog, wrth gwrs, mae darpariaeth cysylltiedig ag ADY a cludiant o'r cartref i'r ysgol yn costio mwy a mwy bob blwyddyn. Mae bellach wedi cyrraedd tua £200 miliwn i'r trethdalwr—arian sy'n dod o gyllidebau addysg. Nawr, efallai y bydd yn syndod i'r criw croch ar ochr arall y Siambr hon, ond dywedodd eu harweinydd ar lefel y DU, pan aeth i Gaint, bod gwariant ar gludiant o'r cartref i'r ysgol yn chwerthinllyd. Mewn gwirionedd, defnyddiodd dermau dyfnach. Dywedodd mai'r ffordd y byddai'n ei dorri fyddai rhoi'r gorau i'w ddarparu, i wneud i rieni yrru neu gerdded eu plant i'r ysgol. Ai dyna bolisi Reform yma, Brif Weinidog, ydych chi'n meddwl?

A, Brif Weinidog, a fyddech chi'n cytuno i ddull mwy synhwyrol, dull mwy deallus, un a gychwynnwyd gan Lywodraeth Lafur Cymru, lle gwnaethom ni gyfansoddi panel arbenigol, grŵp trawsbleidiol traws-adrannol, i edrych ar sut y gallwn ni leihau costau cludiant o'r cartref i'r ysgol tra'n gwella faint o gludiant o'r cartref i'r ysgol y gellir ei ddarparu i bobl ifanc?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I certainly agree with the comments made that there is an ideological drive to push down public transport by the Reform benches, and they don't seem to care who that impacts. I think we have seen in recent weeks around the ALN funding issue that we are able to reach a positive place through co-operation, and I'm always interested in looking at how we can co-operate across the Senedd in finding ways to spend public money well on ALN needs, on public transport and on learner transport. It is through that co-operation that we will get better results.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n sicr yn cytuno â'r sylwadau a wnaed bod ymgyrch ideolegol i wthio trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus i lawr gan feinciau Reform, ac nid yw'n ymddangos bod ots ganddyn nhw ar bwy y mae hynny'n effeithio. Rwy'n credu ein bod ni wedi gweld yn ystod yr wythnosau diwethaf o amgylch pwnc ariannu ADY ein bod ni'n gallu cyrraedd sefyllfa gadarnhaol trwy gydweithredu, ac mae gen i ddiddordeb bob amser mewn edrych ar sut y gallwn ni gydweithredu ar draws y Senedd i ddod o hyd i ffyrdd o wario arian cyhoeddus yn dda ar anghenion ADY, ar drafnidiaeth gyhoeddus ac ar gludiant i ddysgwyr. Drwy'r cydweithrediad hwnnw y byddwn ni'n cael canlyniadau gwell.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Arweinydd y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig, Darren Millar.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Leader of the Welsh Conservatives, Darren Millar.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lywydd. Look, Labour didn't fold, they collapsed. Isn't that the case?

First Minister, people across Wales are facing a cost-of-living crisis, yet senior managers in the public sector and in publicly funded organisations are enjoying pay packets that people in our country could only dream of. And what's really galling is that the worse their organisations seem to perform, the better the pay packet seems to be.

Let's take Transport for Wales, for example. Last year, it was one of the worst performing rail companies across the whole of the United Kingdom in terms of cancellations, yet its chief executive is earning nearly £0.25 million every single year. Then there's Cardiff Airport. It currently receives £20 million per year in annual subsidy from the Welsh Government just to stay afloat, yet its latest financial statements show that its highest paid director received a package of more than £275,000 per year. And in north Wales, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board has the worst performing emergency departments and longest waiting times in the country, yet its chief executive is earning a salary of £262,500 per year. It's scandalous. 

So, do you agree with me, First Minister, that these salaries are now completely out of control, they bear no relationship to the performance of their organisations, and that no-one in the public sector or in a publicly funded organisation should be rewarded for failure?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. Edrychwch, nid ildio wnaeth Llafur, fe aethon nhw ar chwâl. Onid dyna'r gwirionedd?

Brif Weinidog, mae pobl ledled Cymru yn wynebu argyfwng costau byw, ac eto mae uwch reolwyr yn y sector cyhoeddus ac mewn sefydliadau a ariennir yn gyhoeddus yn mwynhau pecynnau cyflog y gallai pobl yn ein gwlad ddim ond breuddwydio amdanyn nhw. A'r hyn sydd wir yn cythruddo yw mai'r gwaethaf y mae eu sefydliadau yn perfformio, y gorau y mae'n ymddangos yw'r pecyn cyflog.

Gadewch i ni gymryd Trafnidiaeth Cymru, er enghraifft. Y llynedd, roedd yn un o'r cwmnïau rheilffordd a berfformiodd waethaf ar draws y Deyrnas Unedig gyfan o ran achosion o ganslo, ac eto mae ei brif weithredwr yn ennill bron i £0.25 miliwn bob un blwyddyn. Yna mae Maes Awyr Caerdydd. Ar hyn o bryd, mae'n derbyn £20 miliwn y flwyddyn mewn cymhorthdal blynyddol gan Lywodraeth Cymru dim ond i barhau i weithredu, ac eto mae ei ddatganiadau ariannol diweddaraf yn dangos bod ei gyfarwyddwr sy'n derbyn y cyflog uchaf wedi derbyn pecyn o fwy na £275,000 y flwyddyn. Ac yng ngogledd Cymru, Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Betsi Cadwaladr sydd â'r adrannau brys sy'n perfformio waethaf a'r amseroedd aros hiraf yn y wlad, ac eto mae ei brif weithredwr yn ennill cyflog o £262,500 y flwyddyn. Mae'n gywilyddus.

Felly, a ydych chi'n cytuno â mi, Brif Weinidog, bod y cyflogau hyn allan o reolaeth yn llwyr bellach, nad oes unrhyw berthynas rhyngddyn nhw â pherfformiad eu sefydliadau, ac na ddylai unrhyw un yn y sector cyhoeddus neu mewn sefydliad a ariennir yn gyhoeddus gael ei wobrwyo am fethiant?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I must say at the outset that there's a real irony here, isn't there, that the Conservatives choose to focus on high salaries when tax cuts for the highest earners are always among the driving forces of the Conservatives' agenda, which does nothing whatsoever to help people in Wales who are living with the challenges of the cost-of-living crisis.

Across the public sector, we need to make sure that we have the right people in the right place. That does absolutely involve paying them the right sums of money. But all I can tell you is that this new Government, through our work on effectiveness and efficiency, will do everything that we can to make sure that the public pound in Wales is driven as far as it possibly can be. Securing that value for money is at the heart of what this Government is trying to achieve for Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae'n rhaid i mi ddweud ar y cychwyn bod yna eironi gwirioneddol yma, onid oes, bod y Ceidwadwyr yn dewis canolbwyntio ar gyflogau uchel pan fo toriadau treth i'r enillwyr uchaf bob amser ymhlith y grymoedd sy'n ysgogi agenda'r Ceidwadwyr, sy'n gwneud dim o gwbl i helpu pobl yng Nghymru sy'n byw gyda heriau'r argyfwng costau byw.

Ar draws y sector cyhoeddus, mae angen i ni wneud yn siŵr bod gennym ni'r bobl iawn yn y lle iawn. Mae hynny yn sicr yn golygu talu'r symiau cywir o arian iddyn nhw. Ond y cwbl y gallaf i ei ddweud wrthych chi yw y bydd y Llywodraeth newydd hon, drwy ein gwaith ar effeithiolrwydd ac effeithlonrwydd, yn gwneud popeth o fewn ein gallu i wneud yn siŵr bod y bunt gyhoeddus yng Nghymru yn cael ei gwthio cyn belled ag y gellir ei gwthio. Mae sicrhau'r gwerth am arian hwnnw yn ganolog i'r hyn y mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn ceisio ei gyflawni i Gymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Look, we all know why you are not in favour of performance-related pay and that's because you'd all be skint, wouldn't you, frankly, if it was based on the performance of your Government so far. Let's look at a decision. You say that you want efficient and fair services for taxpayers, let's take a look at a decision that you took last week, as a Government, on your Government website. On 7 October, you approved a salary of more than £200,000 per year for a chief executive of Natural Resources Wales, and a package that would be worth more than that. That's another organisation that has faced serious criticism over its performance: failures to tackle illegal dumping; slow progress in delivering flood defences; and sewage discharges into Welsh waterways, which people have been protesting outside the Senedd about even today. Yet, your Government has decided to offer its next boss a salary that is much higher than even your own—
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Edrychwch, rydym ni i gyd yn gwybod pam nad ydych chi o blaid cyflog sy'n gysylltiedig â pherfformiad ac mae hynny oherwydd y byddech chi i gyd heb ddimai, oni fyddech chi, i fod yn onest, pe bai'n seiliedig ar berfformiad eich Llywodraeth chi hyd yma. Gadewch i ni edrych ar benderfyniad. Rydych chi'n dweud eich bod chi eisiau gwasanaethau effeithlon a theg i drethdalwyr, gadewch i ni edrych ar benderfyniad a wnaethoch chi yr wythnos diwethaf, fel Llywodraeth, ar wefan eich Llywodraeth. Ar 7 Hydref, fe wnaethoch chi gymeradwyo cyflog o fwy na £200,000 y flwyddyn i brif weithredwr Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru, a phecyn a fyddai'n werth mwy na hynny. Mae hwnnw'n sefydliad arall sydd wedi wynebu beirniadaeth ddifrifol am ei berfformiad: methiannau i fynd i'r afael â dadlwytho anghyfreithlon; cynnydd araf yn cyflawni amddiffynfeydd rhag llifogydd; a gollyngiadau carthion i ddyfrffyrdd Cymru, y mae pobl wedi bod yn protestio amdanyn nhw y tu allan i'r Senedd hyd yn oed heddiw. Ac eto mae eich Llywodraeth wedi penderfynu cynnig cyflog i'w bennaeth nesaf sy'n llawer uwch na hyd yn oed eich—

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cwestiwn, Darren.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: A question, please, Darren.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: These unacceptable salaries for public sector fat cats have gotten out of control and must stop. So, can I ask you today, First Minister: will you introduce a public sector pay restraint Bill to prevent excessive salaries for senior managers paid by the public purse, to make sure that there's fairness for taxpayers and to ensure that pay reflects performance and doesn't reward failure?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r cyflogau annerbyniol hyn i unigolion blonegog y sector cyhoeddus wedi mynd allan o reolaeth ac mae'n rhaid iddyn nhw ddod i ben. Felly, a gaf i ofyn i chi heddiw, Brif Weinidog: a wnewch chi gyflwyno Bil cyfyngu cyflogau sector cyhoeddus i atal cyflogau gormodol i uwch reolwyr a delir o bwrs y wlad, i wneud yn siŵr bod tegwch i drethdalwyr ac i sicrhau bod cyflog yn adlewyrchu perfformiad ac nad yw'n gwobrwyo methiant?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Pay absolutely should reflect performance. But I again point to the irony here. We have to make sure that we get value for money from, yes, at times, high wages within the public sector. But compare like for like. Where were the Conservatives calling for the bankers to pay their part of the bill for the financial collapse that is still causing pain for families in Wales today? Where are the Conservatives when it comes to making sure that public spending is able to help those people in communities the length and breadth of Wales, with two out of every five children in Wales living in poverty? I'm afraid that this is faux outrage from the Conservatives. And on performance-related pay, the Conservatives have precisely nothing to show for 27 years in this Parliament.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Dylai cyflog adlewyrchu perfformiad, yn sicr. Ond tynnaf sylw eto at yr eironi yma. Mae'n rhaid i ni wneud yn siŵr ein bod ni'n cael gwerth am arian o'r hyn sydd, ydyn, ar adegau, yn gyflogau uchel yn y sector cyhoeddus. Ond cymharwch tebyg am debyg. Ble'r oedd y Ceidwadwyr yn galw ar y bancwyr i dalu eu rhan o'r bil am y chwalfa ariannol sy'n dal i achosi poen i deuluoedd yng Nghymru heddiw? Ble mae'r Ceidwadwyr o ran gwneud yn siŵr bod gwariant cyhoeddus yn gallu helpu'r bobl hynny mewn cymunedau ar hyd a lled Cymru, gyda dau o bob pump o blant yng Nghymru yn byw mewn tlodi? Mae gen i ofn bod hyn yn ddicter ffug gan y Ceidwadwyr. Ac ar gyflog sy'n gysylltiedig â pherfformiad, does gan y Ceidwadwyr ddim o gwbl i'w ddangos am 27 mlynedd yn y Senedd hon.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Effeithlonrwydd y Llywodraeth
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Government Efficiency

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 3. Pa welliannau mesuradwy o ran effeithlonrwydd ac effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth Cymru y mae'r Prif Weinidog yn disgwyl eu cyflawni yn ystod y Senedd hon? OQ64721
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 3. What measurable improvements in the efficiency and effectiveness of the Welsh Government does the First Minister expect to deliver during this Senedd? OQ64721

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Our programme for government sets clear priorities. We will drive efficiency and effectiveness by focusing on these priorities, working collaboratively across Government with a clear focus on outcomes for the people of Wales. We're committed to being the most transparent Government since devolution. And the first iteration of our digital dashboard, for example, which measures progress against our top priorities, was issued this summer.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae ein rhaglen lywodraethu yn pennu blaenoriaethau eglur. Byddwn ni'n ysgogi effeithlonrwydd ac effeithiolrwydd drwy ganolbwyntio ar y blaenoriaethau hyn, gan weithio ar y cyd ar draws y Llywodraeth â phwyslais eglur ar ganlyniadau i bobl Cymru. Rydym ni wedi ymrwymo i fod y Llywodraeth fwyaf tryloyw ers datganoli. A chyflwynwyd fersiwn gyntaf ein dangosfwrdd digidol, er enghraifft, sy'n mesur cynnydd yn erbyn ein prif flaenoriaethau, yr haf hwn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
First Minister, taxpayers don't measure Government efficiency by how many strategies, reviews or initiatives you announce; they measure it by what actually improves and what it costs them.

Your Government has promised measurable outcomes, progress milestones, plans for plans, greater productivity and so on, so will you actually put the numbers against those promises? Will you publish clear targets showing how much taxpayers' money you intend to save, and which areas of Government will become more efficient and by when? And when programmes or public bodies repeatedly fail to deliver value for money, will you actually reform, merge or scrap them? Because Government efficiency cannot just mean spending more money more efficiently; sometimes, it actually means having to spend less.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Brif Weinidog, nid yw trethdalwyr yn mesur effeithlonrwydd y Llywodraeth yn ôl faint o strategaethau, adolygiadau neu fentrau yr ydych chi'n eu cyhoeddi; maen nhw'n ei fesur yn ôl yr hyn sy'n gwella mewn gwirionedd a faint mae'n ei gostio iddyn nhw.

Mae eich Llywodraeth wedi addo canlyniadau mesuradwy, cerrig milltir cynnydd, cynlluniau ar gyfer cynlluniau, mwy o gynhyrchiant ac yn y blaen, felly a wnewch chi wir yn rhoi'r niferoedd yn erbyn yr addewidion hynny? A wnewch chi gyhoeddi targedau eglur sy'n dangos faint o arian trethdalwyr yr ydych chi'n bwriadu ei arbed, a pha feysydd o'r Llywodraeth fydd yn dod yn fwy effeithlon ac erbyn pryd? A phan fydd rhaglenni neu gyrff cyhoeddus yn methu dro ar ôl tro â sicrhau gwerth am arian, a wnewch chi eu diwygio, eu cyfuno neu eu diddymu? Oherwydd ni all effeithlonrwydd Llywodraeth olygu gwario mwy o arian yn fwy effeithlon; weithiau, mae'n golygu gorfod gwario llai mewn gwirionedd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, neither does spending less mean that you are being more efficient or more effective, that's what my response would be to that. You spend what you need to spend, not a penny more. You drive that efficiency, you drive that effectiveness. That's the programme that the Government is engaged with now in looking at budgets for the coming years. We have a set budget. Reform voted against fair funding for Wales, but we will work within the budget that we have. And in spending every pound sensibly, in looking at how we get the most out of every pound, that is how we drive outcomes. Because I absolutely agree with the Member that it's not measuring how much you spend, it's what you do with the money. And that also goes on whether you're putting efficiency drives in place for ideological reasons, or whether you're doing it in order to get more out of the system. Let's focus on what we're trying to achieve always for the people of Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, nid yw gwario llai yn golygu chwaith eich bod chi'n fwy effeithlon neu'n fwy effeithiol, dyna fyddai fy ymateb i hynny. Rydych chi'n gwario'r hyn y mae angen i chi ei wario, dim ceiniog yn fwy. Rydych chi'n ysgogi'r effeithlonrwydd hwnnw, rydych chi'n ysgogi'r effeithiolrwydd hwnnw. Dyna'r rhaglen y mae'r Llywodraeth yn ymwneud â hi nawr wrth edrych ar gyllidebau ar gyfer y blynyddoedd i ddod. Mae gennym ni gyllideb benodedig. Pleidleisiodd Reform yn erbyn cyllid teg i Gymru, ond byddwn yn gweithio o fewn y gyllideb sydd gennym ni. Ac wrth wario pob punt yn synhwyrol, wrth edrych ar sut yr ydym ni'n cael y mwyaf o bob punt, dyna sut rydym ni'n ysgogi canlyniadau. Oherwydd rwy'n cytuno'n llwyr â'r Aelod nad yw'n fater o fesur faint rydych chi'n ei wario, mae'n fater o beth rydych chi'n ei wneud gyda'r arian. Ac mae hynny hefyd yn wir o ran pa un a ydych chi'n rhoi ymgyrchoedd effeithlonrwydd ar waith am resymau ideolegol, neu os ydych chi'n ei wneud er mwyn cael mwy allan o'r system. Gadewch i ni ganolbwyntio ar yr hyn yr ydym ni'n ceisio ei gyflawni bob amser i bobl Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Effective Government is underpinned by taking a collaborative, cross-sector and holistic approach to policy development and decision making. It recognises that many of the challenges facing Wales cannot be addressed by individual departments working in isolation. Because for too long, previous Governments have operated in silos, failing to look at the bigger picture and tackle shared challenges through joined-up action. Take prevention, for example. Prevention cuts across health, housing and culture. Food policy connects social justice, public health and rural resilience. Creating high-quality jobs needs co-ordination between the economy and education. So, Prif Weinidog, I'd like to know how this Plaid Cymru Welsh Government is already working collaboratively across ministerial portfolios in a tangible and measurable way that will genuinely make a difference to the lives of the people of Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae Llywodraeth effeithiol wedi'i seilio ar fabwysiadu dull cydweithredol, traws-sector a chyfannol o ddatblygu polisi a gwneud penderfyniadau. Mae'n cydnabod na all adrannau unigol yn gweithio ar wahân fynd i'r afael â llawer o'r heriau sy'n wynebu Cymru. Oherwydd ers rhy hir, mae Llywodraethau blaenorol wedi gweithredu mewn seilos, gan fethu ag edrych ar y darlun ehangach a mynd i'r afael â heriau cyffredin trwy weithredu cydgysylltiedig. Cymerwch atal, er enghraifft. Mae atal yn croestorri iechyd, tai a diwylliant. Mae polisi bwyd yn cysylltu cyfiawnder cymdeithasol, iechyd y cyhoedd a gwydnwch gwledig. Mae creu swyddi o ansawdd uchel yn gofyn am gydgysylltiad rhwng yr economi ac addysg. Felly, Brif Weinidog, hoffwn wybod sut mae'r Llywodraeth Cymru Plaid Cymru hon eisoes yn gweithio ar y cyd ar draws portffolios gweinidogol mewn ffordd wirioneddol a mesuradwy a fydd yn gwneud gwahaniaeth gwirioneddol i fywydau pobl Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
This is a programme of work that we put in place in the early weeks of this new Government. The programme for government is built around a set of priorities. To deliver on those priorities and all those other areas that the Welsh Government is responsible for will take a whole-Government approach. Cross-Government working we really want to be a part of our DNA as a Government.

I tasked the Cabinet Minister for Government effectiveness to ensure that the Government works collectively across portfolios to deliver meaningful outcomes. Here are three examples. On climate change, yes, there's a Minister responsible, but it belongs to all of us, so we've put the structures in place to make sure that we're working collaboratively on climate change. Prevention is another one that cuts across the work of so many departments. Tackling poverty is another one of those.

I'd also make the point, Llywydd, that it's not how we work co-operatively within Government alone that matters. Effective delivery also depends on strong collaboration with others—local government, for example, businesses, the third sector and, crucially, communities across Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae hon yn rhaglen o waith a roddwyd ar waith gennym ni yn ystod wythnosau cynnar y Llywodraeth newydd hon. Mae'r rhaglen lywodraethu wedi'i hadeiladu ar gyfres o flaenoriaethau. Bydd angen dull Llywodraeth Cymru gyfan i gyflawni'r blaenoriaethau hynny a'r holl feysydd eraill hynny y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn gyfrifol amdanyn nhw. Rydym ni wir eisiau i weithio traws-lywodraethol fod yn rhan o'n DNA fel Llywodraeth.

Gofynnais i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros effeithiolrwydd y Llywodraeth sicrhau bod y Llywodraeth yn gweithio ar y cyd ar draws portffolios i gyflawni canlyniadau ystyrlon. Dyma dair enghraifft. Ar newid hinsawdd, oes, mae Gweinidog sy'n gyfrifol, ond mae'n perthyn i bob un ohonom ni, felly rydym ni wedi rhoi'r strwythurau ar waith i wneud yn siŵr ein bod ni'n gweithio ar y cyd ar newid hinsawdd. Mae atal yn un arall croestorri gwaith cynifer o adrannau. Mae mynd i'r afael â thlodi yn un arall o'r rheini.

Byddwn hefyd yn gwneud y pwynt, Lywydd, nad sut rydym ni'n gweithio ar y cyd o fewn y Llywodraeth yn unig sy'n bwysig. Mae cyflawni effeithiol hefyd yn dibynnu ar gydweithredu cryf ag eraill—llywodraeth leol, er enghraifft, busnesau, y trydydd sector ac, yn hollbwysig, cymunedau ledled Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, you've spoken about the importance of improving the efficiency and effectiveness of the Welsh Government. You've even appointed a Minister for the task. My constituents and the people of Wales need more than just warm words, new strategies and talking shops. They actually want to see improvements in the areas that matter most to them and they want to see their money spent wisely. We've all heard about these ambitious targets and pie-in-the-sky plans from your Government. In fact, you've filled 70 pages with pipe dreams and packaged it up as a programme for government full of ideas but very light on delivery. So, First Minister, what specific measurable targets are you going to be setting during this Senedd term to reduce waste, improve productivity, slash NHS waiting lists and improve educational outcomes across the board? Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, rydych chi wedi sôn am bwysigrwydd gwella effeithlonrwydd ac effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth Cymru. Rydych chi hyd yn oed wedi penodi Gweinidog ar gyfer y dasg. Mae angen mwy na geiriau gwresog, strategaethau newydd a siopau siarad ar fy etholwyr i a phobl Cymru. Maen nhw eisiau gweld gwelliannau yn y meysydd sy'n bwysicaf iddyn nhw mewn gwirionedd, ac maen nhw eisiau gweld eu harian yn cael ei wario'n ddoeth. Rydym ni i gyd wedi clywed am y targedau uchelgeisiol hyn a'r cynlluniau breuddwyd gwrach gan eich Llywodraeth. Mewn gwirionedd, rydych chi wedi llenwi 70 tudalen gyda breuddwydion a'i becynnu fel rhaglen lywodraethu sy'n llawn syniadau ond yn ysgafn iawn o ran cyflawni. Felly, Brif Weinidog, pa dargedau mesuradwy penodol ydych chi'n mynd i'w gosod yn ystod y tymor Senedd hwn i leihau gwastraff, i wella cynhyrchiant, i leihau rhestrau aros y GIG yn sylweddol ac i wella canlyniadau addysgol yn gyffredinol? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
We can point to a whole host of targets that are already in place, from the first meaningful economic target that we've had in maybe a quarter of a century, on halving the productivity gap with the rest of the UK within a decade. That's setting our sights high, but we need that kind of target. We know about the targets on the longest waiting times in the NHS. We have a very clear path towards raising standards in numeracy, literacy and so on.

I'd refer the Member to the answer I gave a few moments ago. Yes, we want to be efficient in our use of public money in everything that we do. And yes, we have already found ways that we, I believe, can deliver more for less in a whole host of different ways, and I think that's very important.

But to ideologically drive down spending for the sake of it doesn't help the people of Wales. What helps the people of Wales is using money wisely, carefully and setting a clear trajectory for the kinds of changes that we want to deliver for them. With childcare, we know what it is that we're trying to deliver. We know what we have to do. We're getting on with the job.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Gallwn gyfeirio at lu o dargedau sydd eisoes ar waith, o'r targed economaidd ystyrlon cyntaf yr ydym ni wedi ei gael ers chwarter canrif efallai, ar haneru'r bwlch cynhyrchiant â gweddill y DU o fewn degawd. Mae hynny'n gosod ein golygon yn uchel, ond mae angen y math hwnnw o darged arnom ni. Rydym ni'n gwybod am y targedau ar yr amseroedd aros hiraf yn y GIG. Mae gennym ni lwybr eglur iawn tuag at godi safonau mewn rhifedd, llythrennedd ac yn y blaen.

Byddwn yn cyfeirio'r Aelod at yr ateb a roddais ychydig funudau yn ôl. Ydym, rydym ni eisiau bod yn effeithlon yn ein defnydd o arian cyhoeddus ym mhopeth yr ydym ni'n ei wneud. Ac ydym, rydym ni eisoes wedi dod o hyd i ffyrdd y gallwn ni, rwy'n credu, gyflawni mwy am lai mewn llu o wahanol ffyrdd, ac rwy'n credu bod hynny'n bwysig iawn.

Ond nid yw gyrru gwariant i lawr yn ideolegol dim ond er mwyn gwneud hynny yn helpu pobl Cymru. Yr hyn sy'n helpu pobl Cymru yw defnyddio arian yn ddoeth, yn ofalus a phennu trywydd eglur ar gyfer y mathau o newidiadau yr ydym ni eisiau eu cyflawni iddyn nhw. Gyda gofal plant, rydym ni'n gwybod yr hyn yr ydym ni'n ceisio ei gyflawni. Rydym ni'n gwybod yr hyn sy'n rhaid i ni ei wneud. Rydym ni'n bwrw ymlaen â'r gwaith.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Anghydfod Ymwelwyr Iechyd Cwm Taf Morgannwg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Cwm Taf Morgannwg Health Visitor Dispute

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 4. Pa gamau mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i ddatrys yr anghydfod o ran tâl ymwelwyr iechyd a graddio ym Mwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Cwm Taf Morgannwg? OQ64682 [R]
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 4. What action is the Welsh Government taking to resolve the health visitor pay and grading dispute at Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board? OQ64682 [R]

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I recognise the vital role that health visitors play in supporting children and families across Wales. Responsibility for their pay, grading and employment rests with the health board as the employer. But we have engaged with the health board and the trade union, making clear our expectation that all parties should work constructively towards a swift resolution. We will continue to support those efforts while ensuring appropriate arrangements remain in place to safeguard children and families.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n cydnabod y rhan hanfodol y mae ymwelwyr iechyd yn ei chwarae yn cynorthwyo plant a theuluoedd ledled Cymru. Y bwrdd iechyd fel y cyflogwr sy'n gyfrifol am eu cyflog, eu gradd a'u cyflogaeth. Ond rydym ni wedi ymgysylltu â'r bwrdd iechyd a'r undeb llafur, gan wneud yn eglur ein disgwyliad y dylai pob parti weithio'n adeiladol tuag at ddatrysiad cyflym. Byddwn yn parhau i gefnogi'r ymdrechion hynny gan sicrhau bod trefniadau priodol yn parhau i fod ar waith i ddiogelu plant a theuluoedd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
First Minister, I accept the health visitor dispute began before you took office, but it has continued under your Government, affecting vulnerable children and families in my constituency. In March, Heledd Fychan, who now sits in your Cabinet, asked the previous First Minister to intervene. Luke Fletcher reminded the Government that it was, in his words,

'setting the policy and funding the services.'

Then, on 17 April, you signed a letter calling for band 6 health visitors to be upgraded to band 7. Yet your Cabinet Minister for health continues to describe this as a local employment dispute between Unite and the health board, with no fixed timetable for resolution. First Minister, you now set the policy, you fund the services, and you signed the call for band 7.
